macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street falls as Treasury yields rebound and inflation fears return
items.summary: U.S. stocks declined, with the Dow Jones down 1.31%-1.32%, the S&P 500 off about 0.86%-0.87%, and the Nasdaq lower by about 1.0% as rising Treasury yields and renewed inflation concerns pressured risk assets. Several reports also linked the move to higher oil prices and geopolitical tension involving Iran.

items.title: Treasury doubles buybacks of long-dated U.S. debt to ease yield pressure
items.summary: The U.S. Treasury announced it will double the size of its long-term Treasury bond buybacks, aiming to support liquidity and reduce pressure on the long end of the yield curve. Markets initially welcomed the step, but yields later climbed again.

items.title: Fed minutes signal more tightening could be needed if inflation stays elevated
items.summary: Minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting showed that many participants believed further rate increases may be necessary if inflation does not continue to ease. Other reports said the minutes had limited immediate market impact.

items.title: European markets close lower as oil jumps and bond yields rise
items.summary: European equities mostly finished lower, with the Ibex 35 falling 0.18% to 19,811 points, as oil prices rose on heightened U.S.-Iran tensions and bond yields continued to climb. Investor caution was also shaped by expectations for upcoming inflation data in Germany and the U.S.

items.title: Walmart shares sink after earnings hit U.S. stock sentiment
items.summary: Walmart fell more than 8%-9% in response to its results, adding pressure to a weaker U.S. equity session. Market commentary said the stock's drop contributed to broader caution in consumer and retail names.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin surges past $75,000 as Trump-backed crypto policy boosts market
items.summary: Bitcoin jumped above $75,000 in the past 24 hours, reaching its highest level in months as traders reacted to a White House crypto meeting, President Trump’s push for the CLARITY Act, and Treasury support that helped push yields lower. Ether also rose sharply, and the broader crypto market saw a surge in liquidations as short positions were squeezed.

items.title: Bitcoin tops $71,900 on falling yields and White House crypto optimism
items.summary: Bitcoin rose about 4.1% to more than $71,900 after a meeting between President Trump and crypto industry leaders, alongside Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s move to push U.S. bond yields lower. Bloomberg also reported that a Hyperliquid-related token gained 23% after Trump said the U.S. is considering options for allowing the derivatives platform to operate domestically.

items.title: Crypto market posts broad breakout as Bitcoin, Ethereum and XRP rally
items.summary: The crypto market rose nearly 8% over 24 hours, with Bitcoin reclaiming $70,000 and Ethereum at one point gaining as much as 18%, according to market coverage. The move was linked to Treasury support for the debt market and fresh SEC crypto proposals, which added to the policy-driven rally.

items.title: Bitcoin climbs above $71,000 while liquidations exceed $3.26 billion
items.summary: Bitcoin rose more than 10% to above $71,000 and Ethereum climbed nearly 19% as the rally triggered heavy forced liquidations across exchanges. Coinglass data cited in the report showed more than $3.26 billion in positions liquidated over 24 hours, with short positions accounting for the overwhelming majority.

items.title: Bitcoin briefly surges past $75,500; altcoins also jump
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly traded above $75,500 before easing back, while still holding a strong 24-hour gain and adding roughly $190 billion to crypto market capitalization. The report also said Ethena, Pump.fun, Curve DAO Token and XRP were among the day’s standout gainers.

items.title: Trump hosts crypto executives and urges passage of CLARITY Act
items.summary: President Trump met with cryptocurrency leaders at the White House and publicly pushed Congress to pass the CLARITY Act, reinforcing the market’s policy optimism. Coverage from the event highlighted the administration’s increasingly pro-crypto stance and its immediate impact on prices.

items.title: SEC unveils new crypto-market proposal amid rally
items.summary: Market coverage reported that the SEC unveiled new rules for the crypto market, adding a regulatory catalyst to the day’s price action. The proposal was cited alongside Treasury support and the White House meeting as a key driver of the broad rally.

items.title: Hyperliquid mentioned as U.S. explores allowing derivatives platform access
items.summary: A token associated with Hyperliquid rose sharply after Trump indicated the U.S. was considering options to let the derivatives platform operate in the country. The move was one of the clearest project-specific winners from the day’s policy headlines.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: GTA VI gameplay leak dominates gaming news
items.summary: Multiple reports say new GTA VI gameplay footage has leaked online again, fueling speculation that the uploader may have access to a playable build rather than just recorded clips. Coverage also says the leaks are drawing wider industry attention because of their potential impact on Take-Two and Rockstar ahead of upcoming official promos.

items.title: Take-Two reportedly loses billions after GTA VI leaks
items.summary: Commentary around the latest GTA VI leaks says Take-Two’s market value dropped sharply, with one report estimating roughly $2.8 billion erased in under two days. The claim is tied to investor reaction after the new gameplay footage spread online.

items.title: Riot Games reportedly shuts down 2XKO development
items.summary: GamesRadar reports that Riot Games is ending development of 2XKO this year after the fighting game failed to retain enough players. The final content update is said to arrive in October.

items.title: Microsoft reportedly parts ways with Compulsion Games
items.summary: TheGamer reports that Microsoft is moving ahead with layoffs affecting smaller studios, including Compulsion Games after South of Midnight. The article frames this as another sign of broader restructuring across Xbox-related teams.

items.title: Roblox faces US Senate investigation over child safety
items.summary: A gaming-news roundup says the US Senate has opened a bipartisan investigation into Roblox’s handling of child safety concerns. The probe follows Roblox’s reporting of tens of thousands of suspected child abuse incidents on the platform.

items.title: Sony reportedly reboots Horizon spin-off after negative feedback
items.summary: A gaming-news roundup says Sony is rebooting Horizon Hunters Gathering, the live-service co-op spin-off, after negative playtest feedback. The report says the game is being scaled back and elements of the service model are being reduced.

items.title: Mattel launches new game studio focused on free-to-play projects
items.summary: A roundup video says Mattel has formed Mattel Game Studios, a large new operation targeting free-to-play mobile games and experiences in Roblox and Fortnite. The studio is expected to build around Barbie, Hot Wheels, and other Mattel brands.

items.title: BGMI esports sees major disciplinary and qualification updates
items.summary: An esports roundup highlights a lifetime ban handed to a Tier-1 BGMI competitor, along with updates on standings and teams qualifying for the EWC playoffs. The coverage also mentions broader discussion about BGMI and BGMI Lite potentially sharing a server.

items.title: Epic Games Store offers Cardpocalypse free for a limited time
items.summary: A gaming-news roundup says Epic Games Store made Cardpocalypse free to claim from August 20 through August 27. The offer is part of Epic’s weekly giveaway rotation.
